inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 solve the same problem (wallet resubmission defeating -privatebroadcast) by opposite means: route resubmission through private broadcast vs. suppress it. They were originally banded P1 and P2; they are now both P2 and must be decided together. Review #36330 first as the simpler, more conservative behaviour.

The rebroadcast-privacy cluster overlaps heavily: #36398 (only rebroadcast own txs, default path), #36482 (only announce what was actually added to the mempool), #36380 (-walletbroadcast=initialonly), plus #34533/#36330. #36398 is the broadest and should be reviewed first, since it may subsume or change the shape of the others; #36481 (manual rebroadcast RPC/GUI) is the user-facing mitigation for the recipients #36398 leaves stranded and should be considered alongside it.

Chain: #36442 (represent multipath in one Descriptor) -> #36443 (reconstruct multipath from expansion) -> #36444 (store multipath in wallet). #36443 was P3 while the PR it unblocks was P2; all three are now P2 and must be reviewed in that order.
Chain: #10102 (multiprocess) -> #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect) -> #19461. #19460 cannot land first and inherits nothing beyond scaffolding, so it stays below #10102.
Silent payments: #32966 (receiving) precedes #35302 (sending, which also depends on #35301). Reviewing sending before receiving is wasted effort.

Multisig wizard (#35645) prerequisites #36070, #36143 and #35918 are three slices of the same project and overlap in descriptor/key-expression helper territory; they share a band and should be looked at as one group to avoid duplicated API surface.

Migration-path PRs touch the same code and conflict in intent: #34193 (staged migration with restore-on-failure), #35998 (handle WalletBatch write failures, including in migration), #34909 (move ~800 lines of migration code to a new module) and #35733/#34502 (legacy cleanup). The two correctness PRs (#34193, #35998) should be reviewed before the move-only refactor #34909.
#32993 and #35342 both add wallet fuzz targets; #32993 is the better targeted of the two and #35342 has documented efficacy objections.
#25722 depends on #25665/#26022 and #30343 on #34778/#29256; neither dependency is in this category, so their review value is gated externally.
result.notes: The category is dominated by one theme that the per-PR assessments split inconsistently: five open PRs change wallet rebroadcast behaviour for privacy reasons, originally spread across P1, P2 and P3. Only #36398 affects default configurations and long-standing issue #3828, so it keeps P1; the -privatebroadcast-conditional and opt-in variants are levelled at P2/P3. Otherwise the band structure is: migration/loading data-loss and fund-safety defects at P1, user-visible bugs plus the major perf and privacy features at P2, deferrable fixes and features plus behaviour-neutral refactors at P3, and test-only reorganisation, naming deprecations and explicitly not-for-merge prototypes at P4.
